eyebrow: The CASE expression you already know
code:
SELECT Name, ListPrice,
  CASE WHEN ListPrice > 1000 THEN 'Premium'
       ELSE 'Standard' END AS PriceTier
FROM Production.Product;
caption: A simple two-branch CASE expression.
condition, true_value, false_value -- a direct CASE shorthand.

eyebrow: Nesting IIF is a sign to switch to CASE
code:
-- Works, but gets hard to read fast:
IIF(ListPrice > 1000, 'Premium',
    IIF(ListPrice > 500, 'Mid-Range', 'Standard'))

-- CASE stays clear past two branches:
CASE WHEN ListPrice > 1000 THEN 'Premium'
     WHEN ListPrice > 500 THEN 'Mid-Range'
     ELSE 'Standard' END
caption: Same result either way -- readability is the only real difference.
